linkedin.text:
In 2024, a team showed up to our hackathon with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan. By dusk, they'd shipped a working prototype and won thousands of dollars.

That's how our Future of Data Hackathon team describes 2024.

If you're a student, you want a day like that. You want to build something people will use, with someone who hires watching you work.

So the next year, we capped the student field at 40, in teams of four.

Forty was small enough that every student could get direct mentorship and meaningful access to the executives at the event. It was also large enough to form diverse teams.

Then we lined up two clients. Beginner Track teams were set to build data and AI tools that support cancer research operations at Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory in Newport, KY.

Founded in 1981, the lab maintains over 2 million tissue specimens.

Experienced Track teams were set to work with the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati on AI for member analytics, program scheduling, and outreach.

Each student would build for a client who could use the work, and get direct mentorship while doing it.

Which track would you have picked?

Read the full post: https://disruptionnow.com/blog/40-student-slots-real-world-impact
